policy: Owner C1: compare same-task capability with available alternatives; retire no tool without evidence that its valuable uses are covered.

comparison_design.task: Find at most five bibliographic metadata records about artificial intelligence in healthcare, retaining provider identifiers for follow-up.
comparison_design.same_permission_class: One public read-only query per selected provider; no API key, account email, repository writes, or external action. OpenAlex reported rate-limit usage credits; account-level monetary charge remains unknown.

retrieval_window_utc.note: Provider observations are within one session window but were not simultaneous.

pubmed.reason: The existing PubMed adapter requires a caller-supplied contact_email sent to NCBI. No task-specific contact address was supplied, so none was transmitted.
pubmed.contract_comparison: Reviewed as an alternative, but no same-task quality, recall, or result comparison is claimed.

arxiv_known_id_lookup.comparison: Its exact-ID input cannot discover candidate IDs from a topic query; it remains useful after a record identifier is known.

openalex_known_doi_lookup.comparison: Requires caller-supplied DOI identifiers and returns selected Work metadata; it does not perform text query-to-record discovery.

findings: All three public query adapters completed one bounded same-high-level-task discovery observation and returned five metadata rows, but their query syntax, corpus scope, provider ordering, identifiers, ranking fields, and retrieval times differ.

OpenAlex reported 638997 matching Works for this query, Europe PMC 159566, and arXiv 4563. Provider hit counts have provider-specific definitions and are not comparable measures of recall or corpus completeness.

The observed result sets and provider identifiers differ. This one snapshot does not establish comparative relevance, recall, source quality, availability, cost, or scientific value; no scientific review was performed.
arXiv, Europe PMC, and OpenAlex have distinct source collections and identifier contracts. They can coexist when the task needs those scopes; this evidence does not support retiring any query tool.

OpenAlex search capability already existed in a general client, which returns broader data. The new candidate adds a bounded no-key, no-placeholder-email, metadata-only route; it does not establish a new provider capability.

The existing OpenAlex DOI metadata lookup has a different input and purpose. PubMed same-task comparison remains NOT_RUN because its adapter requires a caller-supplied contact_email, and none was supplied.
The OpenAlex request reported ten keyless rate-limit usage credits used. No API key, account email, or account-specific monetary charge was established.

disposition.reason: The measured providers have different source scopes and identifiers; no paired evidence ranks relevance or establishes that one source covers the other valuable uses. Preserve them as default-off, task-scoped options.
